prompts.text: Which songwriting partnership interests you because the collaborators bring different strengths?
Tell me about hearing that two musicians disagreed creatively and then made something memorable together.
You bring a lyric and I bring a melody, but neither fits the other's first idea. How might we find common ground?
Good collaboration can make a song feel more individual rather than less.
Two musicians building a song in one room or exchanging ideas over several weeks?

What would make you curious about the relationship between a singer and their producer?
A band has four different ideas for how a chorus should sound. What kind of test could help them choose?
Describe discovering that an unexpected guest musician helped shape a favourite recording.
How can musicians keep their own creative voices while building something together?
Have you heard a recording where you could almost imagine the room it was made in?
Tell me about listening to music recorded outdoors and noticing the environment around the performers.
You could record the same acoustic song in a chapel, a living room or a small studio. Which space would you try first?
A perfectly clean recording doesn't always capture the most interesting performance.
Hearing the warmth of a small rehearsal room or the spacious sound of a large hall?
Reverb and room noise can make a recording feel as though it belongs somewhere specific.
What makes you feel close to a performer through a recording even when you aren't there?

Tell me about an artist whose work felt connected to a part of your background you hadn't explored much.
You're making a short musical self-portrait without speaking. What sounds would you choose to represent different parts of your life?

A playlist reflecting the places you've lived or one tracing how your taste has changed with time?

What kind of music helps you feel connected to people or places you don't see often?
Someone assumes your musical taste from where you grew up. How might you explain the difference?
Describe discovering a musical influence you didn't realise had shaped your preferences.

A stripped-back acoustic version or a bold reimagining with an entirely new rhythm?
Changing a song's tempo can reveal meanings in the words that were easy to miss before.
Have you heard an instrumental arrangement that helped you notice the structure of a familiar song?

Comparing the same melody played by three instruments or following one harmony part inside a choir?
Once you learn to recognise a musical pattern, it can start appearing in songs everywhere.
Do you find it easier to hear the structure of a song when you know its lyrics or when it's instrumental?

Describe discovering that a musical passage was more complicated than it sounded at first.
What's one listening skill you'd like a musician to demonstrate for you?
